cirajīvins
(‘those who live eternally’)
------------------------------------------
The Hindu epics and पुराणस् have listed seven persons as ‘cirajīvins’ or ever-living. They are: Aśvatthāma (the son of preceptor Droṇa), बलि (the king of पाताल or the nether world), हनुमान् (the monkey-devotee of राम), Kṛpa (a ब्राह्मण warrior mentioned in the महाभारत), परशुराम (the sage turned killer of the evil kṣattriyas), विभीषण (youngest brother of रावण, the king of लङ्का) and व्यास (the sage and author of the epic महाभारत and the पुराणस्).
To this list should be added the name of मार्कण्डेय, the sage who conquered death through his devotion to शिव.
Due to various reasons as depicted in their stories they obtained the boon of living for ever on this earth, though in a subtle body.
